title: Looking for 2–4 testers for a strategy-backtesting tool (free, no catch, honest feedback wanted)
author: DeliciousEquipment13
selftext:
Hi all — I've built a tool called Atlas Edge and I'm looking for 2–4  people to test it before any public launch.



What it actually is: a backtesting and automation platform. You connect your own IG account, build your own intraday strategy from a library of components (breakouts, trailing stops, filters, etc.), and the platform runs it through a genuinely rigorous statistical validation process — walk-forward testing, placebo controls, realistic cost modelling — before telling you honestly whether it holds up.



What it isn't: a signal service, an "AI trading bot," or anything promising guaranteed returns. It doesn't tell you what to trade. Most strategies people build (including my own, extensively) get correctly rejected — that's the tool working as intended, not a sales pitch gone wrong.



Why I'm posting this: I want people who aren't me actually using it, breaking it, and telling me honestly where it's confusing or annoying, before I open it up more broadly.



What's in it for you:



Free access during this test phase



Direct input into what gets built next



A genuinely rigorous way to test your own trading ideas before risking real money on them



Requirements:  18+, active

If you're interested, comment or DM me and I'll send over the details.

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: The walk-forward and placebo controls are a strong foundation. One failure mode worth testing is feature and parameter selection leakage across folds; logging the exact selection boundary and freezing it before the next window would make rejected strategies easier to diagnose. Marx could use those diagnostics as context rather than treating a backtest score as a signal.

replies.author: DeliciousEquipment13
replies.body: Would you be interested in joining the testing so we can discuss more? I have dm you

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: The separate holdout point is especially important here: if users iterate on a strategy after seeing walk-forward results, the final untouched period should remain hidden until the end. Storing the assumptions, parameter changes, costs, and regime-level results would also make each rejection explainable. That evidence trail is the kind of thing Marx can consume cleanly later.
